claimScope.whyTheDistinctionMatters: ConcHarness builds DoubleOceanAssemblyCandidate with a sine/cosine stand-in as its ContinentField (ConcHarness.continent), so it never exercises ContinentField, the composed DoubleGalleryCandidate, or the E->C->height curve end to end. Citing it as complete-chain evidence would be a false claim. The build/verify scripts now keep the two apart and reject a real-chain probe that reintroduces a stand-in sampler.
claimScope.cancellationNotClaimed: DoubleFullMorphLand serializes mutating state on its own monitor. Concurrent callers COOPERATE by blocking: that is mutual exclusion, not a cancellation API. There is no interruptible checkpoint, no progress handle, and no way to abort an in-flight tile build. The cancel/retry row in ConcHarness measures a harness-owned attempt loop that stops issuing NEW work between attempts; it never cancels work already inside the chain. A passing result must not be read as cancellation support.

realChainEvidence.configDiscipline: config loaded exactly once on the main thread before any worker starts; workers only call e()/height() on pre-constructed objects and never read or write GeoGenesisConfig

verify.concurrencyProbeConfigPolicy: probes-conc (6 files) must contain zero references to GeoGenesisConfig / CommentedFileConfig / TomlFormat; verify.ps1 enforces that as a preflight. probes-realchain is deliberately EXEMPT because it must load the config once on the main thread to build a real ContinentField and HeightCurve. Giving it its own directory is what makes a directory-scoped check correct instead of a blanket ban that would reject the very probe we need.

memoryWitness.claim: GC observation only; NOT a hard memory bound
memoryWitness.noDefaultEntryCap: PerlinScalarCache is a plain WeakHashMap with no ceiling configured. Eviction happens only when a key is collected and the map expunges the stale entry. An earlier revision measured a fixed cap to be actively harmful (one owner graph holds ~181 distinct Perlin instances, so a 512-entry cap produced more evictions than misses); that is why no cap exists by design. A passing result must not be read as an entry bound or as a memory ceiling.
memoryWitness.whyRewrittenNotCopied: The sandbox probe carried a 'legacy' mode that rebuilt the pre-fix IdentityHashMap container and pulled fixtures from ConcHarness, whose continent source is a sine/cosine stand-in. Neither belongs in a preserved artefact, so this is a self-contained fixed-cache-only rewrite that builds the real DoubleFullMorphLand directly.
stageRows: NOTE,heapRetainedIsObservationOnly,no entry cap by design (WeakHashMap default),eviction happens only when a weak key is collected,this run does not establish a hard memory ceiling
